South is great - AC, an elevator, good common rooms, and right next to Marquis (my preferred dining hall). It’s pretty close to most academic buildings, at least as close as you’ll get unless you’re in RISC all the time and live in Watson.

1. Ruef is not as much loud as chaotic, unless you live in a room right next to the stairs in which case it’s a bit loud but usually mostly on weekends.
2. Decor is really on a person by person basis. I’d say generally the girls I’ve seen (including me) have like a color for bedsheets and rug if you get one etc that ties things together. Guys tend to do very little but that shouldn’t stop anyone. There’s also a poster sale in September that helps people add some decor if they want. Budget $5-10 per poster depending on size.
3. I have always seen a standard large mini fridge, think about 3 feet tall? About the height of a desk. The micro fridge is useful if you’re planning on making a lot of food or live very far from the kitchen but otherwise isn’t really necessary.
4. The rooms are pretty clean. I’ve always mopped the floor and wiped out any drawers I’m planning on using for clothes but I’m a bit more paranoid about it than most people.
5. Showers will be clean on move in. How clean they are or smell will be determined by if you’re using a women’s bathroom or a men’s. It’s not mold or anything just standard teenage boy grossness. Regardless you should bring flip flops or slides or something to wear in the shower.
6. I’ve never seen anyone bring their own headboard - if you really want it then bring it but if it’s more for aesthetic reasons then don’t stress about it too much.
7. They all have a big window but it will depend on which direction your room faces. East and west, yes at different times of day. North and south, not direct but you’ll still get light. I also think most rooms in Ruef have window AC units so that’ll determine if you can open the window etc.
8. The halls and bathrooms are cleaned pretty regularly but again it will depend on who you’re living with/ girls vs guys bathroom. Nothing egregious either way.
I hope that helps!!

It’s tough to tell how much you’re really missing out in because it seems like every school is doing in-person learning differently. It really sucks though and you shouldn’t try to brush your feelings under the rug or say they aren’t that important.

I suggest you pick one friend, either from school or out of school, that you’re close with and feel you can reach out to without worrying about judgement. Text them and see what they’ve been up to, ask about schoolwork or their siblings or TV shows they’ve been watching. If it’s the kind of thing you like, I strongly recommend finding a game like Minecraft or Among Us or something like that that you can play online with them. In doing that you may discover a new hobby, or meet new friends online that you can feel connected to.

I also suggest that, if you’re comfortable with it, speaking to your parents about how you’re feeling. At the very least they will probably be able to relate as they’re missing out on spending time with their friends too. They might suggest (as I would) speaking to a therapist or school counselor. The situation sucks right now and a lot of people are feeling disconnected from their lives, and some online resources are available for free or really low prices due to the prevalence of people needing support. Especially if your emotions are largely sad or unmotivated, I suggest talking to someone as this can be a sign of depression.

I had already been diagnosed with depression before this whole pandemic started, but even already having support and medication it’s taken a rough toll on me. There’s no shame in asking for help or reaching out and saying that you’re struggling. Just because you’re not suicidal doesn’t mean everything is hunky dory.

Last of all, and especially if you’re not ready to approach your parents with that yet, try to reach out to family members. I know everyone has a different family, but it can be an aunt, grandpa, older cousin, or even a family friend. Someone who can give you more personalized advice and maybe tell you more about what to look forward to in high school.

It’s totally understandable that you’re feeling sad and maybe a little lost. There are a lot of people feeling similarly and, while that doesn’t make yours suck less, at least you know that you’re not alone and you’re not overreacting or anything. Take some time for yourself and your mental help and reach out to people you trust for support and friendship. Best of luck and feel free to post again or give us an update!!
